operations.name: capacity.get
operations.description: How many places a record of an object with a capacity has left (a ticket type, a class). Staff get places, held (while someone pays), taken (paid), available, and the pool's numbers when the record draws on a parent's places. Customers and the public get only what the object shows: the number left, a low-stock warning, or available / sold out. Read-only; claims nothing.

object.description: An extension object that declares a capacity

status.description: `low` only when the object shows a low-stock warning and few are left

available.description: Places left; null when unlimited. Shown to outsiders only when `show` allows

operations.name: me.deleteAccount
operations.description: Delete your customer account and ask for your personal data to be erased. You are signed out everywhere at once and can no longer sign in. Staff then erase your data, or tell you by email why some of it must be kept, by the due date returned. Asking again changes nothing.

operations.name: me.get
operations.description: Your own Person, as a signed-in customer: your name, primary email and primary phone, and your account's sign-in address (signInEmail, the one the emailed code verified, with signInEmailVerified). Link records kept elsewhere to a customer by signInEmail only: primaryEmail is a contact address staff can change. Read-only.

signInEmail.description: The address you sign in with: the one the emailed code verified, lower-cased. Not the Person's contact email (primaryEmail), which staff can change. The only address to trust when linking records kept elsewhere to this customer.

signInEmailVerified.description: Whether signInEmail was verified by an emailed code. True for every signed-in customer.

operations.name: me.sessions.list
operations.description: The places you are signed in, as a signed-in customer: each session's id, whether it is a browser or an app on a device (with the device's name), when it began, when it was last used and when it expires, and which one is this one. Read-only.

operations.name: me.sessions.revoke
operations.description: Sign out one of your sessions, as a signed-in customer, by its id from me.sessions.list. A session that is not yours is not found.

operations.name: me.signOut
operations.description: Sign out of this session, as a signed-in customer. Your other sessions stay signed in (end them with me.sessions.revoke).

operations.name: me.update
operations.description: Change your own name or primary phone, as a signed-in customer. Only the fields you pass change; pass null to clear one. Your email cannot be changed here. Returns your Person.

operations.name: my.get
operations.description: One of your own records (or one that a record of yours points to, such as your ticket's event), as a signed-in customer, with only the fields you may see. A record that is not yours is not found. Read-only.

object.description: The object, e.g. `person` or an extension object such as `shop.order`

currency.description: For an object that is for sale: the currency every price of it is in (the deployment's one currency), or null until one is set. Absent for any other object.

operations.name: my.list
operations.description: A page of your own records of an object, as a signed-in customer (and the records every signed-in customer may read, where the object shares some, and the ones a record of yours points to, such as your ticket's event): only the records that are yours and only the fields you may see. Filter and sort on those fields; pass nextCursor back as cursor for the next page. Read-only.

object.description: The object, e.g. `person` or an extension object such as `shop.order`

currency.description: For an object that is for sale: the currency every price of it is in (the deployment's one currency), or null until one is set. Absent for any other object.

operations.name: order.cancel
operations.description: Cancel an order. A signed-in customer can cancel their own order while nothing has been paid on it. Staff can also cancel an order that is part paid (a deposit was paid): that gives up its places, and refunding what was paid is a separate step. A paid order is refunded, not cancelled. Returns the order.

refunded.description: What has gone back to the buyer, confirmed by the provider

operations.name: order.checkout
operations.description: Open the payment provider's own page to pay for an order, and get its address to send the buyer to. The host says what is charged: the whole price or the deposit for an order with nothing paid (no amount may be given), or, for a part-paid order, the balance or a part of it of at least the set minimum (`amount`, in the currency's minor unit). The buyer comes back to `returnUrl`, which must be on one of the deployment's listed sites; coming back does not mark anything paid. Only the provider's confirmation does. A guest passes the order's token; a signed-in customer pays their own orders.

token.description: A guest's token for the order

returnUrl.description: Where the buyer comes back to

amount.description: Part-paid orders only: how much to pay towards the balance, in minor units

operations.name: order.get
operations.description: Get one order with its lines: its state, amounts (in the currency's minor unit), what has been paid, the balance and when it is due. A signed-in customer gets their own orders only; anyone else's is not found. Read-only.

refunded.description: What has gone back to the buyer, confirmed by the provider

operations.name: order.start
operations.description: Start an order for one or more records that are for sale, as a signed-in customer, a guest (with an email address) or staff. The host prices it from the records: a caller never sends a price or a total. The order starts pending and is not paid: paying happens on the payment provider's page (order.checkout), and only the provider's confirmation marks it paid. An unpaid order expires after a few minutes. Returns the order with its lines and amounts in the currency's minor unit; a guest also gets `token`, shown once, which is the only way back to the order (order.view).

object.description: The object of the record to buy

lines.description: What to buy. There is no price here: the host reads it from each record, and a price or total sent anyway is ignored.

pay.description: full: pay the whole price now. deposit: pay the deposit now and the balance by its due date, when every line offers a deposit.

email.description: The buyer's email address. Required when the caller is not a signed-in customer; a signed-in customer's order uses their account's address and must not pass one.

refunded.description: What has gone back to the buyer, confirmed by the provider

token.description: A guest's key to this order. Null for everyone else.

operations.name: order.view
operations.description: See one order with the token it was started with (a guest's link from order.start or the confirmation email). The token opens that order only, while it is open and for 30 days after it closes. A wrong id, a wrong token and an old link are all not found. Read-only.

refunded.description: What has gone back to the buyer, confirmed by the provider

operations.name: x.programs.classToday
operations.description: A class type's sessions on a date (default today, UTC), with their plans: every level of every item, typed targets, and the bank exercises. What a coach runs a class from and a member reads before it. Notes for coaches only are left out for members. Read-only. (Extension tool from Programs 0.1.0.)

plan.description: The session of the layout: blocks, items, levels and typed sets

last.description: The sets of the last time this person did it, before this session

operations.name: x.programs.history
operations.description: Every set a person logged of one exercise, oldest first (date, set, level, target and what was done, effort), and their bests at it (heaviest load, most reps, longest time). A member reads their own; staff name the person. At most 2,000 sets; `capped` says when there were more. Read-only. (Extension tool from Programs 0.1.0.)

personId.description: Staff: the person. A member is always themselves.

operations.name: x.programs.logAdd
operations.description: Log one set done on a session: the item (A1), the exercise when the item has more than one, the level taken when it has levels, which set (1, 2, …), what was done (reps, seconds, load) and how hard it felt (RPE). The target is taken from the session's plan, and who recorded it is the caller. A member logs on their own sessions and their class types'; a coach logs for a client (on a class session, naming them). Nobody logs on a session that is not theirs. Returns the set. (Extension tool from Programs 0.1.0.)

rpe.description: How hard it felt, 1 to 10 in halves

personId.description: Staff: the person. A member is always themselves.

operations.name: x.programs.logUpdate
operations.description: Change a logged set's numbers, effort or note. A member changes their own sets only; staff any. The target, the exercise and who recorded it stay as they were. Returns the set. (Extension tool from Programs 0.1.0.)

rpe.description: How hard it felt, 1 to 10 in halves

operations.name: x.programs.progress
operations.description: A person's training at a glance: for each exercise they logged, how many sets, the first and last date, and their bests; and for each of their assignments, sessions planned, done and skipped. Optionally only one assignment. A member reads their own; staff name the person. Worked out over at most 2,000 sets (`capped`). Read-only. (Extension tool from Programs 0.1.0.)

personId.description: Staff: the person. A member is always themselves.

operations.name: x.programs.sessionComplete
operations.description: Mark one of a person's sessions done or skipped (or back to planned). A member marks their own; staff any personal session. A class type's sessions are not marked by members. Made from the session's current state, so two marks at once count once. Returns the session. (Extension tool from Programs 0.1.0.)

plan.description: The session of the layout: blocks, items, levels and typed sets

operations.name: x.programs.sessionGet
operations.description: One session: its plan, the bank exercises it uses with the person's last numbers at each, and the sets logged on it so far. A member reads their own sessions and their class types' (where `personId` is never given); staff read any, and name the person for a class session's logs. Read-only. (Extension tool from Programs 0.1.0.)

personId.description: Staff: the person. A member is always themselves.

plan.description: The session of the layout: blocks, items, levels and typed sets

last.description: The sets of the last time this person did it, before this session

operations.name: x.programs.today
operations.description: A person's own sessions on a date (default today, UTC: pass the person's local date), each with its plan (blocks, items, levels and typed targets), the bank exercises it uses and the numbers of the last time they did each. A member sees their own; staff name the person. A class type's sessions are programs.classToday. Read-only. (Extension tool from Programs 0.1.0.)

personId.description: Staff: the person. A member is always themselves.

plan.description: The session of the layout: blocks, items, levels and typed sets

last.description: The sets of the last time this person did it, before this session

operations.name: x.ticketing.eventsOnSale
operations.description: The events on sale now, soonest first, each with its ticket types (name, price and its currency, sale window, most per order, deposit) and whether places are left. Prices and deposits are in the major unit of `currency` (45.5 is 45.50). For an event page or a list of events. Only what the public may read: an event that is not on sale is not here. Read-only. (Extension tool from Ticketing 0.1.0.)

timeZone.description: The event's IANA time zone, e.g. Asia/Bangkok: show its start and end, and count its days, in this zone. Null only for an event made before events had one.

available.description: Places left, when the type says so

currency.description: The currency the prices are in (ISO 4217): the deployment's one currency, from the host. Null until an admin sets it, and until then nothing can be bought.

available.description: Places left, when the type says so

operations.name: x.ticketing.myTickets
operations.description: The signed-in customer's own tickets: each with its event (id, name, start, end, venue and state, as they are now, whether or not the event is still on sale), its ticket type (id and name), its code and its state (valid, used or void). Only the caller's tickets exist here; a code that is not theirs finds nothing. Filter by event or by code. Read-only. (Extension tool from Ticketing 0.1.0.)

code.description: Only the ticket with this code

timeZone.description: The event's IANA time zone, e.g. Asia/Bangkok: show its start and end, and count its days, in this zone. Null only for an event made before events had one.

eventStatus.description: The event's state now: draft, on_sale, ended or cancelled

operations.name: x.ticketing.orderStart
operations.description: Start an order for tickets: one or more ticket types and how many of each, paid in full or by deposit when every ticket type offers one. A signed-in customer buys as themselves; a guest gives their email address. The host prices the order from the ticket types, refuses a ticket type outside its sale window, over its most per order or without enough places left (with details naming the rule), and holds the places while the order is unpaid. Nothing is paid here: the buyer then calls order.checkout with the order's id (and a guest's token) to pay on the provider's page. Amounts are in the minor unit. (Extension tool from Ticketing 0.1.0.)

email.description: A guest's email address. A signed-in customer passes none.

token.description: A guest's key to this order, shown once (order.checkout and order.view take it)
